title: Biehn Drive extension and sewer deferred
subtitle: Also: Briar Knoll Drive parking ban, Ontario Health service agreement, and site alteration by-law amendment.
overview: The committee's main business was the proposed Biehn Drive extension and trunk sanitary sewer through a provincially significant wetland. After hearing from the City's consultant, a landowner's planner and many residents, the committee recommended deferring the environmental study report to the March 20, 2023 Council meeting {{vote:m4}}. Staff are to report back on how alternative 4 was scored, traffic needs, other servicing and construction options, flooding and road salt, housing supply, and the future Robert Ferry Drive.

Residents asked for a deferral until Robert Ferry Drive connects to Strasburg Road, citing wetland loss, cold-water trout habitat, flooding and traffic data. Staff said the road and sewer are tied to future development, emergency access and transit.

The committee also recommended banning parking on part of Briar Knoll Drive {{vote:m1}}, authorizing an agreement with Ontario Health for the Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement {{vote:m2}}, and adding the Site Alteration By-law to the Municipal Code {{vote:m3}}. These items go to Council for final decisions.

decisions.item: Biehn Drive and sanitary trunk sewer environmental study report
decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the report, and its filing with the Ministry for 30-day review, to the March 20, 2023 Council meeting so staff can review scoring of alternative 4, traffic, servicing options, flooding, salt, housing supply and Robert Ferry Drive.

The committee recommended amending the Uniform Traffic and Parking Bylaw to prohibit parking on the north (even-numbered) side of Briar Knoll Drive, starting 68 m west of Calmcrest Drive and running 29 m west.

The committee recommended authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign the Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement with Ontario Health, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction, and the CAO or Deputy CAO of Community Services to sign related compliance and reporting documents.
The committee recommended amending Chapter 633 (Fill - Dumping Alteration of Grade) of the Municipal Code to include the Site Alteration By-law as set out in Attachment 'A'.

debate: Delegates asked for deferral until Robert Ferry Drive connects to Strasburg Road, arguing recent traffic counts show nearby roads are not overused and a new traffic study should follow. A petition with over 500 signatures was submitted.

Environmental concerns centred on loss of wetland, cold-water brook trout habitat, groundwater recharge, flood risk for homes with high water tables, and road salt reaching groundwater. Staff said salt cannot be fully treated and can only be directed to a stormwater pond.

A delegate proposed directional drilling for the sewer as a lower-impact option at a small extra cost. Staff said it would be examined in the next design phase but some work in the wetland would still be needed, such as maintenance access.

Staff and the landowners' planner said the sewer must follow gravity to Biehn Drive, and an alternative would be a pumping station. They also cited transit, emergency access on a cul-de-sac longer than fire policy allows, and Carondale Drive traffic near a school. Phasing the road was estimated to add about $1 million in throwaway costs.

Councillors asked for more on flooding, salt and emissions with and without the road, alternative servicing, and what happens to Robert Ferry Drive if Biehn Drive is deferred. One councillor said the pipes appear unavoidable but the road is still open to question.
